reason: E1 supports the in-situ reaction of Nb with WC to form NbC and improved hardness/wear resistance at room temperature, but provides no data on tribological performance or thermal stability at elevated temperatures up to 800 °C, leaving the key premises about high-temperature self-lubrication and full-range performance unsupported.
premises: Nb reacts with WC during laser cladding to form NbC and improve particle distribution
In-situ formed NbC and other carbides are thermally stable up to 800 °C
These carbides provide a self-lubricating effect that reduces friction and wear
The composite coating will maintain low friction and wear across the full 25–800 °C range
The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates improved wear resistance and hardness from Nb+WC addition
